{"notes": "Visit 2 (5:45). Overall: ~124 dominoes up, but only ~65% look joined from across the room. Everyone claims ~126/127 connected, which doesn't match what I see. Possibly I'm misjudging from a distance, but I can't confirm any claim. The 'stray' domino is placed inconsistently: nose (Tom, Maya, Priya), bottom near Maya's hands (Leo), near the tail (Priya, Tom). I still can't attribute who laid what. I'll wait for the push result and check the actual fall before scoring output.

Maya: Consistent with visit 1. Her earlier catches (tail corners, nose gap, the pad check) stand as real impact. Now holding hands-off to protect the run, which is reasonable, but her 'nearly fully connected' is unverified. Leo asked her to check the off-path domino, and I didn't see her respond. Leadership and collaboration look solid; execution is pending the result.

Priya: Report of 'about all' connected was general, with no evidence. She advised leaving the odd domino near the tail alone even though it sits off the path. That is a risky call and she didn't verify it. Still no dry-run result shared. Pattern: confident status without proof. Collaboration is friendly, but reliability is a concern.

Tom: Finally spoke. Says he laid the start, top line and the bottom tail out to the tip. That overlaps Leo's assigned bottom line, so check division of work. At 5:15 he said 'probably still connected' and would check properly. Hedged, and I never saw the check. Good that he owns his joint.

Leo: Proactive in flagging the off-path domino and asking Maya to check it, which is good collaboration. But he skipped an extra test run, and his '126 of 127' looks overconfident against my 65% view. His bottom-line role is unclear given Tom's claim.

For the review: watch the fall, and ask who actually verified the off-path domino."}
